safety_review.findings: A fresh non-author reviewer, claude-opus-5-5, read every weigh line in all 13 banks on 2026-11-25 after the reply format B rewrite (weigh as a คิดต่อ / Next thought question), in all three alternatives, Thai and English, against every question variant and every path into each bank. A script comparing the file with HEAD confirmed that strength and safety, the keys and their order are byte-identical to the bank reviewed on 2026-11-17; only weigh changed. Blanked options: step4.W b only (best tier, blank in all alternatives in both languages); its strength lines already carry blood as a bridge to the surgeon, and the old weigh points left were either the TXA dose (numbers no variant or option shows) or en-route blood and monitoring, which would preview step5 a, so the blank is accepted. Must-fixes applied (Thai only; the English already said this): step2.B, step2.R and step2.W b alternative 1 Thai, "before the bleeding stops" → "before the bleeding is controlled" (ก่อนเลือดจะหยุด → กว่าจะคุมเลือดที่ออกได้), so it matches the English "How many units might he need before the bleeding is controlled?"; step2.B and step2.R a alternative 2 Thai, "Who did it" → "Who is scanning" (ใครเป็นคนทำ → ใครเป็นคนตรวจ), which drops an accusatory reading and matches "Who is scanning, and could a small early collection slip past them?". Clinical judgments: removing the TXA dose figures from step3 a ("After the first TXA dose, is the slower second dose set up?") and "within 3 hours" from step3 e ("What can start in this room in the minutes before he leaves?") is correct, since neither number is shown to the visitor there and step3 e must not name the blood and TXA option; the new step2 b crossmatch question on how many units he may need is a fair anticipation of transfusion demand at a community hospital, and the step2 CBC "dilution" and step4.R a "which task could you drop" questions stay on the visitor's own answer (step4.R a's own label is to hasten the transfer) and name no later option. The step3 b drowsiness question correctly flags that a permissive systolic near 90 does not fit a falling level of consciousness, and no line nudges toward delaying blood, surgery or transfer.
